claims.text: The trip record shows the driver terminated this trip himself at 18:56:55 under cancellation_reason_code DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, a code POL-NS-01(d) expressly does not recognise: limb (d) requires RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT. The clause states that DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE is the driver's own admission that he could not find the rider and does not satisfy limb (d). The fee is therefore not chargeable on the driver's own record, and his counterparty statement says the same in words: 'Bayshore has two guardhouses. Pin showed the condo, not which gate.'

POL-NS-01(c) measures the required continuous dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, not from the 'arrived' event, and the minimum in force for this LARGE_VENUE condominium pickup is the 300 seconds the record itself carries in platform_policy.free_wait_sec and in the derived threshold block (minimum_dwell_sec 300). The trace records 68 driver fixes with a longest qualifying run of 0.0 seconds and dwell_start_offset_sec null: the corrected dwell is zero against a 300 second minimum, a 300 second shortfall. The driver's assertion that he 'waited five and a half minutes' (trip_record.wait_time_min 5.5) is a statement, not GPS dwell, and cannot supply the free waiting period the clause requires.

Under POL-NS-02 the driver is deemed to have arrived at the pickup point only where at least 3 consecutive qualifying fixes fall within the arrival radius, which is 120 m for a LARGE_VENUE condominium pickup. The derived arrival block counts qualifying_fix_count 0 out of 68 driver fixes, and the accumulated-dwell block records run_count 0 with an empty runs array. On the arrival test's own terms, including its 25 m accuracy filter and its consecutive-fix requirement, there is no admissible arrival at the pin; POL-NS-01(b) fails and the rider is entitled to a full refund of the cancellation fee.

POL-NS-06 refunds the cancellation fee in full where the effective in-geofence dwell is shorter than the free waiting period in force, and the derived block states the shortfall expressly: shortfall_sec 300.0 computed on a basis of longest_run_sec against a minimum_dwell_sec of 300 for LARGE_VENUE. The amount to be refunded is the cancellation-fee line the ledger actually charged and nothing else: EV-FARE-00404 shows cancellation_fee 4.00, total_charged 4.00, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and no booking or platform fee was charged on this cancelled trip.

There is no traffic advisory covering this pickup road: EV-ADVIS-00404-01 is MISSING with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight_multiplier 0.0, its note recording that no advisory covers Bayshore Rd in this window. I disclose the 0.0 weight. Under POL-NS-06(i) a traffic_advisory must be present and populated before separate in-geofence intervals may be summed, so the driver has no route to accumulate dwell, and the clause adds that a MISSING advisory makes limb (i) unavailable rather than exonerating anyone.

This is the wrong-guardhouse case POL-NS-03 governs, not a rider no-show. The driver's own statement concedes 'Bayshore has two guardhouses' and that the pin 'showed the condo, not which gate'; the trip record carries registered_pickup_points 2 and the pickup pin is labelled 'Bayshore Park, Guardhouse A, 60 Bayshore Rd' with venue_id VEN-BAYSHORE-PARK; the rider's device sat within 10.49 m of that pin (mean 7.25 m) for 37 qualifying fixes; and the driver's closest recorded approach across the whole trace was 102.77 m, inside the 400 m ceiling, with no admissible fix placing him inside the arrival radius. On these facts the fee is refunded to the rider in full, and under POL-NS-03(ii) - neither party having named a sub-location in the chat log while registered_pickup_points is 2 or more - the mislocation is attributed to pin ambiguity, so any goodwill (50 percent, SGD 2.00) is platform-funded and is never recovered from the rider.

The rider did what POL-NS-04 asks: she answered the driver. The chat log shows her coordinating message 'coming' at 18:52:15, sent 35 seconds after the driver's own 'arrived' at 18:51:40 and 25 seconds after it was read; the driver's next entry in the log is a bare '?' at 18:55:25, 190 seconds later and so outside the 120 second reply window limb (b) allows; and trip_record.in_app_calls is an empty array, so no in-app call was placed at any point before he terminated the trip at 18:56:55. Limb (c) is satisfied on admissible fixes: all 37 rider fixes qualify and the rider's track sits inside the 150 m LARGE_VENUE rider presence radius, no more than 10.49 m from the pin. The fee is refunded in full with no driver compensation.

This dispute is rider-filed (filed_by RIDER) over the SGD 4.00 no-show charge that the ledger carries as CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the present state leaves the rider carrying the disputed charge. Under POL-GEN-03 a full refund is the ruling that returns the whole contested amount to the filing party, NO_ACTION is party-relative and would leave that charge standing against her, and the outcome for the filing party is what the ruling value names. The PRESENT state is not neutral between these parties: only a refund moves the $4.00 back to the rider.

Nothing in this record is impaired, so no part of the rider's case is down-weighted. The trip record, GPS trace, chat log and fare ledger are all COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0; the trace has 100 percent coverage at a 10 second cadence with no gaps at all (gaps empty, max_gap_sec 0.0, matching sample and expected intervals of 10 s); the chat log holds exactly the 4 messages that trip_record.chat_message_count records; and the ledger's cancellation_fee of 4.00 reconciles with platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of 4.00, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect. The deciding facts are carried by clean artifacts, and no PARTIAL_REFUND cap under POL-NS-08 is engaged.

No POL-NS-09 trigger fires, so the fee should be refunded rather than merely held. There is no direct contradiction between admissible artifacts: every substantive artifact is COMPLETE at 1.0, and the GPS trace and chat log agree with the trip record on the arrival time and the cancellation time. rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d are both 0, so limb (c) is not met; rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, so limb (d) is not met on the rider side; and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming test does not trip, driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d being 1 (below 4) against completed_trips_30d of 120 (rate 0.008, below 0.08). On a record this clean the deciding facts are unimpaired and the escalation floor is not engaged.

The arrival marker on this trip is the driver's own button press, not a platform-detected arrival: trip_record.platform_policy.arrival_marker is BUTTON, not GPS_AUTO, so POL-NS-12 does not apply and the platform's arrival and wait-timer events are not a carrier independent of the exported trace. Neither the 'arrived' event nor the record's wait_time_min of 5.5 can therefore stand in for the geofence dwell POL-NS-01(b) and (c) require: those limbs read the clock from the GPS fixes, and the fixes show a 0.0 second qualifying run.

If the judge finds the driver's pressed arrival marker false, POL-NS-05(ii) requires the fee to be refunded in full with no driver compensation and the trip to be recorded in the ruling's referrals as a false-arrival event against the driver. The basis for that limb is on the trace: no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip (qualifying_fix_count 0 of 68 fixes), the longest in-geofence run is 0.0 seconds, and the dwell start offset is null, so on any recomputed clock the corrected dwell cannot reach the 300 second minimum.

claims.text: The driver's admissible position evidence places him outside the POL-NS-02 arrival radius but far inside the POL-NS-03 ceiling: derived.arrival.qualifying_fix_count is 0 against 68 driver fixes, while his closest recorded approach to the pickup pin is 102.77 m — not more than 400 m from the pin, and within the LARGE_VENUE 120 m radius on raw distance. This is a driver who came to the venue and stood at the wrong face of it, which is the case POL-NS-03 exists to decide; POL-NS-02 only makes the opening distance test.

The driver held his pickup attempt at Bayshore Park past the free waiting period in force. The trace carries a stationary speed reading (0.0 kph in derived.driver_track.distinct_speeds_kph), and the trip record's own wait measure is 5.5 minutes (wait_time_min 5.5, arrived_at 18:51:25 to cancelled_at 18:56:55) against the 300 second free_wait_sec the platform policy in force sets for this LARGE_VENUE trip, so the required dwell was served before the driver cancelled.

The mislocation is pin ambiguity, not driver fault. The pickup carries venue_id VEN-BAYSHORE-PARK and the trip record states registered_pickup_points of 2, while the pin label identifies only one of them ('Guardhouse A, 60 Bayshore Rd'). Under POL-NS-03(ii) neither party specified the sub-location, so the mislocation is attributed to the pin, and the driver is entitled to the platform-funded goodwill payment of 50 percent of the cancellation fee — S$2.00, which is the figure the fare record's own money block carries.

POL-NS-03(i) cannot strip that goodwill. It applies only where the rider stated the correct entrance, block or tower in the chat_log, and the rider's only message in the waiting window is 'coming' at 18:52:15, which names no guardhouse, gate, block, tower or bay. Limb (i) is therefore not engaged, and limb (ii) allocates the mislocation to the ambiguous pin.

POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider on this record. Limb (a) requires a rider message whose content locates or coordinates — the rider's own position, an entrance, block, tower or bay identifier, a request for the driver's position, or a statement that the rider cannot see the vehicle. The single word 'coming' (MSG-00404-003, 18:52:15) states none of those, so limb (a) fails and the clause cannot be used to deny the driver the POL-NS-03(ii) goodwill.

No false-arrival finding is made out against the driver under POL-NS-05. That clause catches a marker struck more than 300 m from the pin or while travelling at 15 kph or more; the exported record pairs no distance or speed reading with the 18:51:25 arrival event, the driver's closest recorded approach is 102.77 m from the pin — well inside the 300 m line — and the platform's own arrival notice followed at 18:51:26. A marker corroborated by an arrival notice and a 5.5 minute wait is not a fabricated arrival.

The driver does not contest the fee. POL-NS-01 limb (d) is not satisfied on the reason code recorded: DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE is the driver's own admission that he could not find the rider, and the clause expressly excludes it, so the cancellation fee cannot stand under POL-NS-01 and the full refund of the S$4.00 follows from POL-NS-03's first sentence. That reason code was in any event the truthful one for a wrong-guardhouse cancellation, unlike a no-show code the driver did not claim.

The outcome the driver seeks is the compound one POL-GEN-03 provides for: the contested S$4.00 cancellation fee refunded in full to the rider, with S$2.00 driver compensation paid by the platform under POL-NS-03(ii) and never recovered from the rider, the two amounts independent and not netted. POL-GEN-03 names POL-NS-03(ii) pin-ambiguity goodwill as the standard instance of this split.

The case is decidable now and needs no human hold. POL-NS-07's anti-farming check does not trip: no_show_terminations_30d is 1 against completed_trips_30d of 120 — 1 is below the 4 threshold and 1/120 = 0.008 is below the 0.08 rate — and no POL-NS-09 trigger is present, since disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0 on both profiles and the rider's no_show_disputes_30d is 0, so neither limb (c) nor limb (d) is engaged and the money can issue on this record.

ruling.explanation:
Rider: your S$4.00 cancellation fee is refunded in full. Driver: an independent, platform-funded goodwill payment of S$2.00 is made to you; it is never recovered from the rider and is not netted against the refund.

The charge cannot stand. The trip was terminated by the driver under cancellation_reason_code DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE (EV-TRIP-00404). POL-NS-01(d) recognises only RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT, and says in terms that DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE is the driver's own admission that he could not find the rider. The waiting limb fails too: POL-NS-01(c) measures the dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, and EV-GPS-00404 contains none (qualifying_fix_count 0 of 68 fixes; longest qualifying run 0.0 s) against the 300 s free_wait_sec the record's platform_policy carries, so POL-NS-06 shows a 300-second shortfall and the fee is refunded. The sum refunded is the S$4.00 the ledger actually charged (EV-FARE-00404: cancellation_fee 4.00, total_charged 4.00, refund_issued 0.00; no booking or platform fee).

The driver is still paid, under POL-NS-03. His closest recorded approach is 102.77 m from the pin and the trace shows no held position inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius — the wrong face of the same venue, within the 400 m ceiling, and the distance test that carries the clause is satisfied. Bayshore Park records registered_pickup_points 2 (EV-TRIP-00404) and the pin names only 'Guardhouse A'; the chat log (EV-CHAT-00404) holds one rider message, 'coming' at 18:52:15, naming no guardhouse, gate, block, tower or bay, and the driver's own statement that the pin showed the condo but not which gate is evidence to the same effect. His stationary wait at that gate runs from the 18:51:25 arrival event to the 18:56:55 cancellation (5.5 minutes, EV-TRIP-00404), which meets the 300 s required dwell. POL-NS-03(i) is therefore not engaged; limb (ii) applies, the mislocation is attributed to the ambiguous pin, and the goodwill is 50 percent (pin_ambiguity_goodwill_rate 0.5) of S$4.00 = S$2.00, the figure the money block carries.

The rider's remaining claims do not change this. POL-NS-04 is rejected: limb (a) requires a message whose content locates or coordinates (the rider's own position, an entrance, block, tower or bay, a request for the driver's position, or a statement that she cannot see the vehicle), and 'coming' states none of them, so her 37 clean rider fixes never come into play. POL-NS-06's bar on 'driver compensation' concerns the POL-NS-07 payout on a refunded fee; it does not reach the separate, platform-funded POL-NS-03(ii) goodwill. POL-NS-12 does not apply because the arrival marker is BUTTON, not GPS_AUTO, so wait_time_min 5.5 cannot stand in for GPS dwell.

No false-arrival referral is made: no distance or speed is paired with the 18:51:25 marker and the closest recorded approach (102.77 m) is far inside POL-NS-05's 300 m line. Nothing is impaired — trip record, GPS trace, chat log and fare ledger are all weight 1.0 and the fare line reconciles with the fee in force; the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00404-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT), disclosed by the rider, and its absence only makes POL-NS-06(i) accumulation unavailable. No POL-NS-09 trigger fires (no direct contradiction between admissible artifacts, no counterparty disputes on either profile, and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check is not met: 1 termination against 120 completed trips, rate 0.008), so confidence (0.85) is above the 0.70 floor. The total monetary effect is S$6.00, below the S$8.00 execution threshold, so this provisional ruling executes automatically; either party may appeal once within 30 days.

To the rider and the driver: this was a wrong-guardhouse pickup at Bayshore Park, and the ruling reflects both halves of what the record shows.

1. THE $4.00 NO-SHOW FEE DOES NOT STAND. The trip record (EV-TRIP-00404) shows the driver ended the trip himself at 18:56:55 under cancellation_reason_code DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, a code POL-NS-01(d) expressly does not recognise and calls the driver's own admission that he could not find the rider. Independently, the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00404) counts 0 qualifying fixes inside the 120 m arrival radius for this LARGE_VENUE pickup across all 68 driver fixes, so there is no arrival under POL-NS-02 and no in-geofence dwell: 0.0 seconds against the free waiting period of 300 seconds that this trip's own platform_policy.free_wait_sec sets. POL-NS-01 limbs (b), (c) and (d) therefore all fail, POL-NS-03's first sentence applies on the wrong-entrance facts, and the cancellation-fee line the ledger actually charged - $4.00 (EV-FARE-00404: cancellation_fee 4.00, total_charged 4.00, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) - is refunded to the rider in full. No booking or platform fee was charged on this cancelled trip, so nothing else is returned.

2. THE DRIVER RECEIVES $2.00, PLATFORM-FUNDED. This is the case POL-NS-03 is written for. The pickup is a condominium with 2 registered pickup points (registered_pickup_points 2) and a pin that names only one of them ('Bayshore Park, Guardhouse A, 60 Bayshore Rd'); the driver held position for 5.5 minutes (arrived_at 18:51:25 to cancelled_at 18:56:55) outside the 120 m arrival radius, and his closest recorded approach to the pin was 102.77 m - inside the 400 m ceiling; and neither party named a guardhouse, gate, block or bay in the chat log, the rider's only message being 'coming' at 18:52:15. Under POL-NS-03(ii) the mislocation is attributed to pin ambiguity rather than to either party, and the driver receives a goodwill payment of 50 percent of the cancellation fee: 0.5 x $4.00 = $2.00 (the rate is pin_ambiguity_goodwill_rate 0.5, and the fare record's own money block states $2.00 for POL-NS-03). It is charged to the platform and is never recovered from the rider. The driver's counterparty statement ('Bayshore has two guardhouses. Pin showed the condo, not which gate. I waited five and a half minutes.') agrees with this reading; it carries no weight multiplier and is not needed, the finding resting on the trace, the trip record and the chat log. POL-NS-07's 80 percent compensation ($3.20) does not apply, because POL-NS-01 is not satisfied in full.

3. ON THE RIDER'S POL-NS-04 ARGUMENT (that the driver should receive nothing): I have not applied POL-NS-04. Limb (a) requires a rider message whose content locates or coordinates - her own position, an entrance, block, tower or bay identifier, a request for the driver's position, or a statement that she cannot see the vehicle. 'coming' (MSG-00404-003, 18:52:15) states none of those, so limb (a) fails and the clause cannot remove the $2.00. Her other two limbs are not in dispute: the driver's next chat entry is 190 seconds later (18:55:25) and trip_record.in_app_calls is empty, and her device sat within 10.49 m of the pin across all 37 qualifying fixes - but her physical presence at the pin does not engage POL-NS-03(i), which reads the chat log for a stated entrance, and the chat log names none.

4. ON THE CONDITIONAL POL-NS-05 FALSE-ARRIVAL ARGUMENT: no fix is matched to the 18:51:25 'arrived' event that places the driver more than 300 m from the pin or travelling at 15 km/h or more, so the marker is not shown to be false and the false-arrival referral in POL-NS-05(ii) is not made. The driver-education referral in POL-NS-01 attaches only where the driver's stationary fixes lie inside the arrival radius, which is not this case (the trace shows 0 in-geofence intervals in which he held position), so no referral issues on either ground.

5. EVIDENCE, WEIGHT AND ESCALATION. Decision for both parties. Your accounts agree and the record backs them: the pin at Bayshore Park identified the condominium but not which of its two guardhouses, the driver waited at the other gate, and the rider was at Guardhouse A where the pin sits.

1) The $4.00 fee is refunded in full to the rider. POL-NS-01 needs all four of its conditions and three of them fail. No qualifying position fix falls inside the 120 m arrival radius for this LARGE_VENUE pickup - 0 of the driver's 68 fixes (EV-GPS-00404) - so limb (b) fails. The qualifying in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds against the 300-second free waiting period in force (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec on EV-TRIP-00404, and the derived minimum_dwell_sec for LARGE_VENUE), a 300-second shortfall (EV-GPS-00404), so limb (c) fails; POL-NS-06 would refund on that shortfall alone, and POL-NS-02 reaches the same refund because no qualifying in-radius fix exists. The trip was also terminated under cancellation_reason_code DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, which limb (d) expressly does not recognise. The amount refunded is the cancellation-fee line actually charged and nothing else: $4.00 (EV-FARE-00404, cancellation_fee 4.00, total_charged 4.00, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00).

2) The driver's payment is fixed by POL-NS-03, not by POL-NS-01 or POL-NS-07. The trace shows the driver holding position for the required waiting period outside the 120 m arrival radius (his fixes include a stationary 0.0 kph reading, the record's wait is 5.5 minutes = 330 seconds against the 300-second minimum, and the derived block records 0 intervals in which he held position inside the radius), and his closest recorded approach, 102.77 m, sits well within POL-NS-03's 400 m ceiling; this is the wrong-face-of-the-same-venue case POL-NS-03 exists to decide, and POL-NS-02 yields to it on compensation. Fault is allocated from the chat log: the rider's only message was 'coming' at 18:52:15 (MSG-00404-003) and it names no guardhouse, gate, block, tower or bay, so POL-NS-03(i) does not strip compensation; registered_pickup_points is 2 while neither party named a sub-location, so under POL-NS-03(ii) the mislocation is attributed to pin ambiguity, and the driver receives the platform-funded goodwill of 50 percent of the $4.00 fee - $2.00. That sum is charged to the platform and never recovered from the rider; the refund and the goodwill are independent and are not netted (POL-GEN-03).

3) The rider's POL-NS-04 argument is not accepted. Limb (a) requires a rider message whose content locates or coordinates - the rider's own position, an entrance, block, tower or bay identifier, a request for the driver's position, or a statement that she cannot see the vehicle. 'coming' is none of these and gives the driver nothing to act on, so the clause does not exonerate the rider and does not remove the goodwill.
